content: The following studies and findings provide insights into the diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment of liver fibrosis and chronic hepatitis B (CHB): 1., 2009). 2., 2013). 3. Discrepancies between transient elastography and liver biopsy in assessing liver fibrosis in CHB patients have been analyzed (Kumar M et al., 2013). 4. Transient elastography has been evaluated as a tool for assessing hepatic fibrosis in CHB patients (Kwok R et al., 2009). 5. Non-invasive models have been compared for predicting early liver fibrosis in HBeAg-negative CHB patients (Lee IC et al., 2011). 6. Non-invasive markers of liver fibrosis have been validated and compared in West African CHB patients (Lemoine M et al., 2014). 7. The diagnostic accuracy of transient elastography versus the AST-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) in assessing liver fibrosis in CHB patients has been studied, particularly in primary care settings (Lesmana CRA et al., 2011). 8. Serum markers have been validated for fibrosis staging in CHB and hepatitis C patients (Li J et al., 2014). 9. Retrospective evaluations of APRI and AST/ALT ratios have been conducted to assess liver fibrosis and cirrhosis in CHB and hepatitis C patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (Lin CS et al., 2008). 10. Different APRI thresholds have been analyzed for predicting liver fibrosis in CHB patients, considering age as a categorical marker (Liu HB et al., 2011). 11. Seven non-invasive models have been evaluated for staging liver fibrosis in CHB patients (Ma J et al., 2013). 12. The FIB-4 index has been assessed for diagnosing mild fibrosis in CHB patients (Mallet V et al., 2009). 13., 2009). 14. Transient elastography has been compared to liver biopsy for assessing fibrosis in HIV/HBV co-infected patients (Miailhes P et al., 2011). 15. A multicenter Canadian study has evaluated transient elastography for non-invasive liver fibrosis assessment (Myers RP et al., 2010). 16. Biochemical markers have been used to predict liver histological lesions in CHB patients (Myers RP et al., 2003). 17. Longitudinal assessments of liver stiffness using transient elastography have been conducted in CHB patients treated with nucleoside analogs (Ogawa E et al., 2011). 18. Antiviral therapy has been shown to reduce liver stiffness in CHB patients (Osakabe K et al., 2011). 19. Transient elastography has been evaluated in everyday clinical practice for CHB patients (Sinakos E et al., 2011). 20. The role of FibroTest-ActiTest in predicting histological fibrosis and activity in children with CHB has been studied (Sokucu S et al., 2010). 21., 2010). 22. Acoustic radiation force impulse (ARFI) imaging has been introduced as a new modality for evaluating liver fibrosis (Sporea I et al., 2010). 23. The enhanced liver fibrosis test has been compared with transient elastography for identifying liver fibrosis in CHB patients (Trembling PM et al., 2014). 24. APRI, FIB-4, and Forn’s index have been evaluated for their diagnostic value in liver fibrosis in CHB patients (Ucar F et al., 2013). 25. FibroTest-ActiTest has been compared with histopathology for demonstrating fibrosis and necroinflammatory activity in CHB and hepatitis C patients (Uyar C et al., 2010). 26. Dual cut-off transient elastography has been validated for assessing liver fibrosis in CHB patients (Vigano M et al., 2011). 27. FIB-4 and APRI have been compared in Chinese HBV-infected patients with normal or mildly elevated ALT levels (Wang H et al., 2013). 28. Routine parameters have been used to predict significant fibrosis and cirrhosis in HBeAg-negative CHB patients (Wang Y et al., 2013). 29. A non-invasive algorithm combining transient elastography and serum tests has been developed for advanced liver fibrosis in CHB patients (Wong GLH et al., 2010). 30. Alanine transaminase and HBV DNA levels have been evaluated for predicting liver cirrhosis in HBeAg-negative CHB patients using transient elastography (Wong GLH et al., 2008). 31. On-treatment monitoring of liver fibrosis using transient elastography has been studied in CHB patients (Wong GLH et al., 2011). 32. A simple non-invasive model has been established and validated for predicting significant liver fibrosis in CHB patients (Wu SD et al., 2012). 33. Serum ceruloplasmin levels have been found to negatively correlate with liver fibrosis in male CHB patients, leading to a new non-invasive model for predicting fibrosis (Zeng DW et al., 2013). 34. Non-invasive assessment of liver fibrosis using combined serum aminotransferase/platelet ratio index and hyaluronic acid has been studied in CHB patients (Zhang YX et al., 2008). 35. A simpler score using routine laboratory tests has been developed to predict liver fibrosis in CHB patients (Zhou K et al., 2010). 36. Serum levels of tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-1 have been correlated with liver fibrosis in CHB patients (Zhu CL et al., 2012). 37. FibroScan has been prospectively evaluated for diagnosing hepatic fibrosis in CHB patients (Zhu X et al., 2011). 38. Elastography, serum marker scores, and histology have been compared for assessing liver fibrosis in HBV-infected patients in Burkina Faso (Bonnard P et al., 2010). 39. The performance of 11 biomarkers for liver fibrosis assessment in HIV/HBV co-infected patients has been evaluated (Bottero J et al., 2009). 40. The reproducibility of transient elastography in evaluating liver fibrosis in chronic liver disease patients has been studied (Fraquelli M et al., 2007). These studies collectively highlight the advancements in non-invasive diagnostic tools, the role of serum markers, and the impact of antiviral therapies in managing liver fibrosis and CHB.
